open_points.subject: create replay recognition and check precedence
open_points.text: A01 says a repeat passes stages (1) to (4), then "No other check of stage (6) is made again for a repeat"; A04 says "Only an action that passes all six may be a repeat".
open_points.question: At what point is an existing request id recognised as a repeat, and which lifecycle or conflict checks run before that repeat is answered?
options: Recognise it after stage 4 and run only the repeat-specific checks A01 names
Run all six stages before recognising it
Recognise it before the staged checks, then apply a separate replay check sequence
open_points.default_guess: Recognise it after stage 4 and apply exactly the additional archived/type checks stated by A01.

open_points.subject: owner session cookie scope
open_points.text: The cookie is sent "only to Registry's own origin", but no cookie Domain, Path, SameSite rule, dedicated host requirement or request-origin check defines that boundary.
open_points.question: How is the own-origin restriction enforced, especially when another origin shares Registry's host name?
options: Use a dedicated host plus a host-only cookie and restricted Path
Validate Origin/Host on every owner-interface request in addition to a host-only cookie
Treat same-host sibling origins as allowed cookie recipients
open_points.default_guess: Use a dedicated host, a host-only Secure HttpOnly SameSite cookie, a restricted Path, and server-side origin validation.

open_points.subject: consumption of a pending confirmation
open_points.text: A submission uses the confirmation after session and CSRF checks "whatever the answer — a value bound to another action included".
open_points.question: Does any submitted invalid or random confirmation value consume the session's actual pending confirmation, or only a value that matches that pending one but is bound to the wrong action or inputs?
options: Any post-CSRF confirmation submission consumes the pending confirmation
Only submission of the pending one-time value consumes it
A mismatched value is refused and clears the pending confirmation without treating it as used
open_points.default_guess: Only a constant-time match of the pending one-time value consumes it; mismatched random values leave it pending.

open_points.subject: confirmation expiry boundary
open_points.text: A confirmation value "is valid only in that session, for 10 minutes" without defining validity at exactly the ten-minute instant.
open_points.question: Is a confirmation accepted when now equals shown_at plus exactly 10 minutes?
options: Valid only while now is strictly earlier than shown_at plus 10 minutes
Valid through the exact ten-minute instant
Round time before comparing
open_points.default_guess: Valid only while now is strictly earlier than shown_at plus 10 minutes.

open_points.subject: audit sequence reservation failure
open_points.text: Registry records a number in the instance marks "before the entry commits", while numbers are "never reused" and the next entry continues from the marks.
open_points.question: What happens when the marks advance but the state change and audit-entry transaction then fails: is the unused number permanently skipped, is the mark rolled back, or must the whole operation stop until the mark and transaction can be reconciled?
options: Permanently skip the reserved number
Roll back the mark to avoid a gap
Use a crash-consistent protocol that exposes neither state until both are durable
open_points.default_guess: Permanently skip the reserved number and allow gaps, while never reusing it.

open_points.subject: concurrent audit-entry commits
open_points.text: The text requires "for entries e1 written before e2: e1.sequence < e2.sequence" but only says each number is put in the marks before its entry commits.
open_points.question: How are unrelated concurrent state changes ordered so that sequence-number allocation and transaction commit cannot occur in opposite orders?
options: Serialize every audit-writing transaction globally
Permit commit order to differ and define sequence order as allocation order
Reserve numbers concurrently but delay commits until sequence order permits them
open_points.default_guess: Serialize every transaction that writes an audit entry through one instance-wide audit sequencer.

open_points.subject: validation of unpicked import records
open_points.text: Rule 1 says the mapping shows "every malformed record and every id that conflicts", while rule 3 says records only of unpicked projects "are neither checked, shown as conflicts nor imported".
open_points.question: Are malformed records and conflicts outside the picked projects reported and allowed to block confirmation?
options: Ignore all records belonging solely to unpicked projects
Validate and show the whole file but block only on picked records
Any malformed record anywhere refuses the file
open_points.default_guess: Ignore records belonging solely to unpicked projects, except for enough top-level parsing to identify project ownership.

open_points.subject: import reference graph
open_points.text: A record is malformed when "it names a project or room the file does not hold", but the State 1 imported models define rooms and pointers as naming projects and define no imported record that names a room.
open_points.question: Which record kinds may name a room, and what exact referential-integrity graph must the import validate?
options: Only rooms and pointers name projects; remove the room-reference check
The file format has additional room references that must be added to the model
Pointers may optionally name rooms and that fact must be modelled
open_points.default_guess: Only rooms and pointers name projects; no imported Registry record names a room.

open_points.subject: contents of the displayed import mapping
open_points.text: The mapping lists ids, statuses, rooms, pointers, names, aliases and Customers, yet the accepted import also stores each project's object, revisions and source instants; the consequence says the owner sees "exactly what will arrive".
open_points.question: Which imported facts must be displayed and bound into the confirmation, particularly the object's address, kind and characteristics and the kept source instants?
options: Show and bind every fact that will be stored
Show only the listed summary while silently importing the remaining source facts
Show all personal and identity facts but omit mechanical revision and instant facts
open_points.default_guess: Show and bind every personal, identity, relationship and lifecycle fact; mechanical source instants may be shown in a detailed section but must still be covered by the file digest.

open_points.subject: imported project display names
open_points.text: A16 defaults to "its v1 name and no alias unless the owner gives others", while R0-82 says a display name never names a person and State 1 says projects imported under a person's name "are renamed in the import itself".
open_points.question: Must the owner provide a replacement display name for an imported project whose source name violates the naming rule, even though Registry does not inspect names semantically?
options: Require an explicit replacement for every picked project
Allow the source name unchanged because the rule binds only the owner
Require an explicit acknowledgement or replacement, with semantic compliance remaining the owner's duty
open_points.default_guess: Require the owner to submit a display name for every picked project rather than silently defaulting it from v1.

open_points.subject: migration closure marker and failed transaction
open_points.text: Rule 7 records the closure in the instance marks before the transaction, while rule 9 says "nothing of a refused attempt remains" and the required test says a failed transaction leaves "no closure"; A18 later recreates a missing store closure from those marks.
open_points.question: If the closure mark is durable but the import transaction fails, is the import permanently closed on restart or may it be retried?
options: Write the closure mark only after the transaction commits
Use an atomic prepare/commit marker that distinguishes an incomplete import
Treat the durable mark as success and reconstruct the closure despite the failed transaction
open_points.default_guess: Use a prepare/commit marker and regard only a committed marker paired with the committed store transaction as closure.

open_points.subject: concurrent import confirmations
open_points.text: Registry "checks again" and writes the closure in the import transaction, but no rule serialises two confirmations that both observe the closure absent.
open_points.question: What guarantees that two owner sessions cannot both commit different imports concurrently?
options: Serialize all import confirmations instance-wide
Enforce a unique closure with serializable transaction isolation and make one confirmation lose the race
Allow both transactions when their records do not conflict
open_points.default_guess: Use an instance-wide serializable closure check-and-create so exactly one confirmation can commit.

open_points.subject: backup immediately after import
open_points.text: A16 says the post-import run occurs "so a backup holding the import exists", while A18 says a backup may fail, is deleted when its check fails, and Registry keeps serving.
open_points.question: Is a successful checked backup required before the import is reported accepted, or is the backup merely attempted after the already-accepted import?
options: Import success waits for a successfully checked backup
Import commits and reports success even if the backup attempt fails
Import commits but Registry stops serving until a backup succeeds
open_points.default_guess: The import commits independently; the immediate backup is attempted and failure is reported without reversing the import.

open_points.subject: first creation of the production store
open_points.text: The store "must open for reading and writing and carry the store version of the running release" and another version fails, but no rule says how a new instance with no store obtains its first store.
open_points.question: May Registry initialise an absent empty store at first start, or must release installation create and version it before Registry starts?
options: Registry creates and versions an absent store on first start
The release installation must create the store before start
A separate explicit initialise command creates it
open_points.default_guess: The release installation creates and versions the store; ordinary start never creates one implicitly.

open_points.subject: missing instance marks
open_points.text: "The instance marks there are made at the first start; marks that cannot be read fail the start." A missing marks file can therefore mean either a genuine first start or loss of marks from an established instance.
open_points.question: How does Registry distinguish first start from deletion or loss of the marks, so it does not reset the audit counter or migration closure?
options: Create marks only when both the store and backup location are demonstrably new and empty
Reconstruct marks from the store and backups when missing
Always treat missing marks as first start
open_points.default_guess: Treat missing marks as first start only with a new empty store and no backups; otherwise fail startup for recovery.

open_points.subject: backup after a missed 03:00 run
open_points.text: A run missed while stopped is made at next start "if no backup was made that UTC day", without saying whether that day is the missed schedule's day or the later startup day.
open_points.question: If Registry was stopped at yesterday's 03:00 and starts today before 03:00, does it immediately make yesterday's missed backup or wait for today's scheduled run?
options: Make one backup immediately at startup
Wait for today's 03:00 run
Attempt one backup for every missed day
open_points.default_guess: Make one backup immediately at startup, then do not run again that UTC day.

open_points.subject: retry of a failed daily backup
open_points.text: There is "at most one run per UTC day", but a failed run leaves no backup and is "tried again at the next run"; startup also runs when no backup was made that day.
open_points.question: May a restart later on the same UTC day retry a failed run, or is the next attempt always on the next day?
options: No second attempt that UTC day
Retry at every restart until a checked backup exists
Permit one scheduled attempt and one explicit retry per day
open_points.default_guess: No automatic second attempt that UTC day; retry at the next day's run unless the owner explicitly invokes recovery.

open_points.subject: automatic backup during post-restore reconciliation
open_points.text: A restored instance is first started owner-only for re-erasure, while rule 1 may make a missed backup when it next starts and rule 10 provides no flag that reconciliation is in progress.
open_points.question: Can the restored instance create a fresh 30-day backup containing personal data that should already have been erased before the owner finishes reconciliation?
options: Suppress all backups in a restore-reconciliation mode until the owner completes it
Allow the startup backup and rely on the owner to delete it
Require reconciliation to be performed offline before Registry starts
open_points.default_guess: Require an explicit restore-reconciliation mode that disables backups and service tokens until completion.

open_points.subject: completion of restore reconciliation
open_points.text: The owner must reconcile state "before configuring the tokens and starting it again", but Registry "cannot list them, enforce them or tell when this is done".
open_points.question: What evidence or gate establishes that reconciliation is complete before service and agent access resumes?
options: An explicit owner-recorded completion marker checked at normal startup
An offline administrative procedure with no Registry-enforced gate
A signed reconciliation manifest listing the applied current states
open_points.default_guess: Require an explicit completion marker or reconciliation manifest before a non-owner-only start.

open_points.subject: scope of post-restore reconciliation
open_points.text: Rule 10 says to bring each Customer and project to "erased, restricted, ended or not", which does not state how post-backup project archiving, anonymisation, whole deletion, customer corrections, or other accepted changes are handled.
open_points.question: Which classes of changes after the backup must be replayed or reconciled before normal service resumes?
options: Only retention and data-rights states named in rule 10
Every externally recorded accepted change after the backup
Retention states plus project archive, anonymisation and deletion, but not ordinary business corrections
open_points.default_guess: Reconcile all externally recorded erasures, restrictions, relationship states, project archive/anonymisation/deletion and audit-erasure cutoffs; other lost changes remain declared data loss.

open_points.subject: reconstructing MigrationClosure from instance marks
open_points.text: A18 says that when "the marks hold" a migration closure, Registry writes it into the store, but M10 requires its instant, owner principal, confirmation id and file digest, while A15 describes the marks only as holding audit sequence information.
open_points.question: What closure facts do the instance marks hold, and what exact MigrationClosure is reconstructed after restoring a backup from before the import?
options: Store the complete M10 closure in the marks
Store only an irreversible imported flag and reconstruct a reduced closure
Store a committed closure record plus its audit-entry data in a separate durable journal
open_points.default_guess: Store the complete committed M10 closure, including digest, instant, principal and confirmation id, in a crash-consistent instance journal.

open_points.subject: removed artifact types after rollback or old-release restore
open_points.text: A22 says a removed type's name "is never declared again", while A18 permits a backup to be started by "the release that made it"; that older release may still declare the removed type.
open_points.question: After restoring or rolling back to an older release, may that old release publish or withdraw a type removed by a later release?
options: Rollback to a release declaring a removed type is forbidden
Owner-only restore may run the old release but all writes stay disabled until migration to the current release
The old release may use its historical vocabulary, so removal is not globally permanent
open_points.default_guess: Run an old release only in owner-only recovery mode with artifact writes disabled, then migrate to a current release before serving.

open_points.subject: caller values in interpreted queries or commands
open_points.text: A19 permits a caller value to fill "a value place of a query or command", while A21 defines the injection category as "no input becomes query, command, template or other interpreted structure".
open_points.question: Does A21 prohibit passing caller data as a bound query or command argument, or only prohibit caller data from controlling interpreted structure?
options: Bound values and command arguments are allowed; only structure is prohibited
No caller value may enter any query or command at all
Queries allow bound values but operating-system commands may receive no caller values
open_points.default_guess: Interpret A21 as prohibiting control of interpreted structure while allowing safely bound value positions.

open_points.subject: security review of uploaded-file isolation
open_points.text: The review catalogue requires "path ownership, never executed, storage isolation, who may retrieve it" for files, while A16 says only that the file is kept in an owner session and never in the store; it gives no rule for a disk path, permissions, retrieval or crash cleanup.
open_points.question: If uploaded files are materialised outside memory, what isolation, ownership, retrieval and cleanup rules make the files_artifacts review complete?
options: Keep uploads only in memory
Use Registry-owned private temporary files accessible only through the same owner session and delete them on session end, restart and crash recovery
Leave temporary-file handling to the backend
open_points.default_guess: Use Registry-owned private temporary files with restrictive permissions, no download operation, same-session access only, and startup cleanup of abandoned files.
